newsitem.title: USA: Individual sees breakeven in Q2 '98-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Individual sees breakeven in Q2 '98-analyst.

text.p: Individual Inc's move to sell its recently acquired Freeloader unit frees the company to focus on its core subscription business and should help speed it to profitablity, Hambrecht & Quist analyst Jim Petit said.

Company officials told analysts in a call held Thursday after its fourth quarter earnings that, if it can dispose of assets that drag on earnings, it may reach breakeven in terms of profitability by the second half of 1998, Petit said.
Earlier, the Burlington, Mass.-based company reported a fourth quarter net loss of $0.41 per share compared with a $0.18 per share in the final quarter of 1995.

Individual also said it was in preliminary talks on the outright sale of its Freeloader unit, which it acquired in June 1996 for about $38 million. Alternately, it said it would consider the sale of a stake in the unit to outside investors.

Pettit said Individual's effort to dispose of Freeloader reflects the company's desire to put an unsuccessful acquisition behind it and allow it to meet the profitability requirements investors have demanded of it more quickly.
"I think that clearly we have an abrupt change to focusing on ROI (Return On Investment)," Pettit said of Wall Street's often dim view of profitless Internet stocks like Individual.
"I think news of the possible disposition of Freeloader is a positive for the stock," Pettit said. "Clearly the acquisition was not a successful one and there are some skeletons in the wake."
"If there have been steps that have hurt their earnings profile, they are taking steps to address that," he said.
Individual stock has only recently recovered from a selloff that occurred after a breach occured over acqusition strategy between the company board and founder Yosi Aram.

The company, which provides personalized electronic information delivery, went public in the spring of 1996. It had traded as high as 24, but fell to under four dollars as the struggle for control of the company played out in late summer.
Its share rebound in recent weeks conincided with the introduction of a new version of its products to work on Lotus Notes. The stock closed at $10 Thursday.
As a result of Individual's recent track record with its information subscription business, he said he was considering a new estimate for the 1998 year of $0.05 to $0.10 per share.
Pettit holds a buy rating on the stock. "I've been saying they are going to be a $15 to $20 stock by the end of the year," he said.
